findings.evidence: Container: toast; Placement: in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks
findings.fix: Present this as a modal dialog that persists until dismissed, matching the Placement and Signal description already given, rather than a self-clearing toast.
findings.violation: A fully blocking failure (an expired reset link that prevents completing the password reset at all, described as a centered dialog that blocks the field) is tagged as a self-clearing toast, which could disappear before the reader reads the one message explaining why they cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again.
findings.fix: Add a short reason the 30-character limit exists (e.g. what field or system it feeds), or drop the claim that a reason is missing if none applies.
findings.violation: States a field-length limit the reader will meet again with no reason attached, and knowing the reason would cost nothing to add.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Add a brief acknowledgment of the loss (e.g. an apology or an explicit statement of what was lost) alongside the contact-support instruction, rather than stating the loss and the instruction with no softening.
findings.violation: Reports a completed, unrecoverable loss as a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what that loss costs the reader, even though no other block on this screen offers a way forward and the suggested fix is none.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read. Change this file to one of those formats and upload it again, or select a different receipt.
findings.fix: Validate the file's format as soon as it is selected and warn before submission, rather than waiting for on-submit to report it.
findings.violation: Fires only on-submit for a predictable mistake (wrong file format) that the product already knows at file-selection time, with nothing earlier in the flow warning the reader before they submit.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page
findings.fix: Move the message to sit directly beside or below the password field it concerns, instead of at the top of the form.
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a long form rather than beside the password field it concerns, requiring the reader to scroll up and away from the field to read it.
